_comment_file_servers: Workstation SMB/FTP goes to these only (modules/resolver.file_servers); the firewalls used to draw the destination from all of internal_servers. FS01/FS02/FILE01 addresses are simulator assignments in the 10.0.20.0/24 server subnet, not owner-confirmed.
_comment_server_roles: Internal DNS name -> address (modules/resolver._internal_zone). Pinned so no two roles share an address and vcenter matches esxi_config.vcenter_ip. Names not listed fall back to the positional pick over internal_servers. Appended internal_servers entries (10.0.20.20 and up) keep every earlier index stable.
_comment_domain_controllers: domain_controllers: the five DC addresses the firewall modules always fell back to (DC01-DC05), unchanged so base-estate traffic keeps its baseline. domain_controller_hosts: every DC with its site; DC06-DC16 sit in the site server subnets under 'sites'. New hires' Windows DC events and SMB/LDAP traffic go to their own site (session_utils.site_dc / site_dc_ip / site_file_servers).

_estate_generator._comment: Estate expanded by _local_validation/estate_generator.py (a local tool, not in the repo); do not run it on this file again.

management_plane._comment: Device administration baseline shared by the firewall modules (modules/mgmt_plane.py). Admin logins from outside admin_subnet, SNMP from anything but snmp_pollers and config reads by anyone but backup_account are the management-plane threats.

exfiltration_destinations._comment_direction: direction is the curated upload/download role of an entry and defaults to 'both', which is what almost every entry here genuinely is: you upload a file and someone downloads it, that is the product. Only tag an entry when one direction is not credible. It replaced an arbitrary alphabetical split of this list (sorted()[:12] were downloads, [12:] uploads) that left anonfiles, gist, gofile, dropbox, drive.google and box permanently unreachable for uploads. Pastebin and GitHub Gist are text-sized, so a multi-GB download from them is not credible; everything else stays 'both'.

infoblox_threats._comment_generated_share: Fraction of threat-domain draws that are GENERATED by modules/threat_domains.py instead of taken from the pools below. The curated pools remain the head, so an operator hunting by hand still has names they can type; generated domains are the tail that stops a long run beaconing to the same 25 hosts. Family tokens such as command-control and phishing-kit are preserved verbatim because correlation rules match them as literals. 0 disables generation.

zscaler_config._comment_locations: One Zscaler location per office site (same ten as the office egress pools), so location-level events never name a site ExampleCorp does not have. Denver and Sydney used to be here and match no office.

panw_ngfw_config._comment: Palo Alto Networks NGFW (PAN-OS) traffic logs, CEF over syslog to the Broker VM Syslog Collector (Format=CEF). Lands in panw_ngfw_traffic_raw. Threat mix is the module's _DEFAULT_THREAT_EVENTS; override event_mix.threat to retune.
panw_ngfw_config._comment_syslog_hostname_format: What PAN stamps in the syslog header HOSTNAME field (Device -> Setup -> Management -> Syslog HOSTNAME Format): 'hostname' uses the firewall name, 'ipv4-address' uses mgmt_ip.
panw_ngfw_config._comment_threat_severity_format: THREAT logs: 'number' sends the documented $number-of-severity (1-5) as severity and the word as vendor_severity; 'word' sends the word as severity (the live CLCS column). threat_signatures adds signatures whose Threat ID is known: {key: [id, name, severity, category, subtype]}.
panw_ngfw_config._comment_zones: Optional zone overrides: {name: {hosts: [ips], cidrs: [networks], interface: ethernet1/N}}. Default zones: untrust (non-RFC1918), dmz (published servers), identity (domain controllers), database, servers (internal_servers), users (everything else internal).
panw_ngfw_config._comment_rarity_horizon_days: Rare-event budgeting: every analytic NOT high-volume threat event is capped so its EXPECTED count is <=1 per this many days at the Realistic gate cadence (threat_generation_levels.Realistic seconds = 360 threat slots per 30 days); the freed probability mass flows to _HIGH_VOLUME_EVENTS (port_scan, port_sweep, failed_connections, large_upload https/smtp/ftp, spam_bot, crypto_miner, torrent) in proportion to their classic weights, so the threat pie stays the same size. The six recurring_/ddns daily events are exempt (they are claimed once per UTC day via _due_daily by design, not weight-sampled). Realistic yields <=1 per event per horizon; Extreme (4320 slots/30d) scales every cap proportionally to ~12. 0 disables budgeting and restores the classic fixed weights. Insane always keeps classic weights -- it is a stress mode.
panw_ngfw_config._comment_emit_rt: Emit the CEF rt receipt-time key. Not a PAN traffic-log field (live CLCS rows have rt=null) and ignored for _time on the Syslog-Collector custom-format path; opt in only for consumers that read rt.

okta_config._comment_app_entitlements: Which SSO apps a user is assigned (modules/okta_sso.user_apps): every user gets 'core' plus their department's list plus 1-3 picks from 'optional', fixed per user. Benign sign-ins draw from that set, so a user reaching an app outside it is a genuinely new app for them. Apps in okta_sso_apps that no list names are still valid targets for threat scenarios.

vmware_esxi_config._comment: VMware ESXi host syslog. PLAIN syslog (Format=Raw), not CEF. Broker VM Syslog applet: Protocol=TCP, Format=Raw, Vendor=VMware, Product=ESXi, listening on syslog_port. Lands in vmware_esxi_raw; the Marketplace 'VMware ESXi' content pack supplies the parsing + modeling rules (regexcapture -> parsed_fields -> XDM identity/user/process + Virtualization Stories). Threat mix is the module's _THREATS table.
vmware_esxi_config._comment_event_interval: Default seconds between events for this source (~0.01/s). A real ESXi host is quiet — outside the ambient vpxa poll it changes state rarely — so it defaults far below the usual 1/s. The dashboard reads this at module load (overrides the module's DEFAULT_EVENT_INTERVAL and the global base_event_interval_seconds); operators can still raise the rate per run.
vmware_esxi_config._comment_syslog_port: Dedicated collector port — plain syslog has no in-body routing key, so ESXi is separated from the other syslog sources (cisco_asa 1514, apache 1515, infoblox 1516) BY PORT. Configure a Broker VM Syslog collector on 1518 with Vendor=VMware Product=ESXi Format=Raw.
vmware_esxi_config._comment_mgmt_ip: Loopback is what hostd records for local/console (DCUI/esxcli) auth; remote logons carry the client IP from the session context, the ops-team jump hosts (management_plane), or an external pool.
vmware_esxi_config._comment_vcenter: The managing vCenter Server. vpxa is present on these hosts, so they are vCenter-managed; vCenter drives the host as the built-in 'vpxuser' account (the bulk of hostd logins on a managed host).
vmware_esxi_config._comment_backup: VM backup proxy (NFC/VDDK) that snapshots and reads whole VMs on a schedule. The benign baseline the vm_disk_export threat stands against.
vmware_esxi_config._comment_disabled_accounts: Accounts that still exist but are disabled (NoAccess/locked). A login attempt against one is logged as 'account is disabled' — distinct from an unknown user.
vmware_esxi_config._comment_former_accounts: Deleted/offboarded accounts. A login attempt surfaces as an unknown user (SSH 'Invalid user' / console 'no such user').

windows_events_config._comment_delivery: Buffers and sender settings -- none of these caps volume. Workers wait when a buffer is full instead of dropping. Windows VOLUME is set by wks/dc_interval_multiplier: at 1.0 (production pacing) the 265 workstations send ~484 events/s (~42M/day) using ~22% of one CPU core. Measured ceiling of the single simulator process: ~2,500 events/s. output_queue_size must exceed events per drain interval or it becomes a ceiling.

endpoint_cap._comment: At most `active` Windows workstations generate events on a given day: the `core` hosts every day (all base-estate workstations come first), the rest a different deterministic draw each UTC day from the remaining onboarded hosts. Keeps per-host density and thread count bounded at 5,000 users while hosts keep (re)appearing. active: 0 disables the cap.

packs.description: Scenario 18 - Domain Dominance (Phish -> AD Recon -> Kerberoast -> DCSync -> Lateral -> Persistence). 4-hour day with Okta/Windows/Infoblox/Zscaler baseline.
Scenario 19 - Beaconing Implant (DNS C2 -> DNS tunnel -> web exfil -> FW egress -> service persistence). 4-hour day with Infoblox/Zscaler/FortiGate/Windows baseline.
Scenario 20 - Server Breach -> Cloud Takeover (Apache exploit -> reverse shell -> DNS exfil -> S3 exfil). 4-hour day with Apache/Infoblox/AWS/Zscaler baseline.
Scenario 21 - Cloud Ransomware (brute force -> admin -> stop logging -> exfil -> S3 encrypt + ransom). 4-hour day with AWS/Okta/Zscaler baseline.
Scenario 22 - Perimeter Intrusion (port scan -> denied inbound -> VPN brute force -> web exploit). 4-hour day with Cisco ASA/FortiGate/Apache/Zscaler baseline.
Scenario 23 - Identity Attack -> Cloud (Okta MFA-fatigue + Tor login -> AWS SAML federation -> privesc -> exfil). 4-hour day with Okta/AWS/Zscaler baseline.

user_behavior._comment: department_affinity biases destination/domain/volume choice toward each user's department so peer-group analytics has a signal. It is a weighting offset, never a partition: 0.0 = pure per-user (previous behaviour), 1.0 = a department shares one centre. Every destination stays reachable at any setting.

onboarding._comment: Profiles with a start_date are pre-provisioned new hires: they exist in the directory but generate no activity before that date (UTC), so the estate grows ~50 genuinely first-seen users a day. enabled: false makes everyone active at once.

monthly_rotation._comment: Rotates which users are busy each UTC calendar month, always from user_profiles. core_pct% of users are active every month; of the rest, monthly_pct% are drawn afresh each month (seeded by seed + YYYY-MM, so restarts within a month give the same set). quiet_share of picks still come from the whole roster so rotated-out users never look dormant. New hires stay active for new_hire_grace_days after start_date. novelty gives users newly rotated in a first-seen app, sometimes a colleague's workstation (host_pct, used on host_prob of their Windows picks) and a trip_days trip to an office in another country (trip_pct). month pins the period ("YYYY-MM") for testing. Set enabled to false for output byte-identical to before rotation existed.

domain_corpus._comment: Real long-tail domains (Tranco top-1M, pay-level) for the rare tail of benign DNS (Infoblox, Check Point) and web (Zscaler) traffic. A small config pool only makes a domain rarely picked; over a long run UEBA learns it as normal. Rarity needs cardinality. benign_domains stays the per-user head. tail_share = fraction of benign lookups drawn from the tail. Ranks tail_start_rank..tail_end_rank are used; filter_unsafe drops adult/gambling/warez. Cached under domain_cache/ (gitignored) and refreshed after cache_ttl_hours at startup. Set pinned_list_id (e.g. "GQNVK") for the same tail across restarts. Offline: falls back to the config pool, /api/health warns.
domain_corpus._comment_exfil_tail_share: Fraction of EXFIL destinations (Zscaler data_exfil, dlp_threat, large_download) drawn from the tail instead of exfiltration_destinations. Separate from tail_share because the two model different anomalies: a curated hit is a famous file-sharing site (pastebin/mega/anonfiles) where the anomaly is that a corporate user pushed 400MB to it, and low domain cardinality is correct; a tail hit is a host nothing else in the run resolves, which is how attacker-controlled and compromised-site exfil looks. Uploads to the curated file-sharing pool stay dominant at 0.30. Tail hits are labelled Miscellaneous or Unknown / General Browsing, never Online Storage / File Transfer. Set 0 to disable.
